speech: Binary search is an algorithm we use daily. Imagine that you're writing an essay but need to look up a word in a dictionary. Flipping open the dictionary about halfway would determine if you need to look in the front or back half of it. After cutting down pages by half several times, you'd eventually find the page that you want. How is what you just described about finding a number in a sorted list the same or different compared to searching for a word in a dictionary in this way?

Binary search is similar to how we naturally navigate to a page in a textbook. It would be quick to flip open the book about halfway, check the page number, and see if you need to move forward or back in the book based on where you already are. You'd repeat that cutting down process until you found the page you want. How does navigating to the page compare to what you just described about finding a number in a sorted list? Why is it the same or different?

Binary search is similar to scrolling for a song in a very large alphabetical music playlist on a streaming service. Swiping down and stopping your phone's scroll about halfway, you'd check what letter of the playlist you're in, then decide if you need to move up or down the playlist from there. Why is finding the song in this way the same or different compared to what you just described about finding a number in a sorted list?

Binary search is similar to being at an arcade finding your name on the high scorers list. The machine displays a list of the top 100 player's high scores ordered alphabetically by the player's name. Your eyes naturally check about halfway and depending on your name, you know whether to check earlier in the scorer's list or later. You'd continue this halfway cut down process until your name is found. How does finding your player's high score in this way differ from what you just described about finding a number in a sorted list? Why is it the same or different?

Binary search operates similarly to finding your flight on an airline's flight status board. Your eyes naturally scan the alphabetical destination cities about halfway and depending on where you're traveling, you know whether to check earlier or later on the board. You'd continue this process to find your destination city instead of going through the status board city by city (one by one). How is this algorithm of finding a destination city the same or different from the one you just described about finding a number in a sorted list?
